events.title: FOMC October meeting — hold expected, December hike priced
events.why_it_matters: The Fed is expected to hold at 3.75%–4.00%, but sticky inflation and a resilient economy keep a December hike firmly on the table, making the statement and Warsh's tone the key macro event of the window.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the statement drops easing bias and whether Warsh explicitly validates the ~90% December hike probability.

events.title: US Q3 GDP advance estimate
events.why_it_matters: Atlanta Fed GDPNow has cut Q3 growth to 3.5%, and the first print will test whether the soft-landing narrative survives hot inflation and weak housing.
events.what_to_watch: Consumption and inventory contributions; a sub-3% print would pull forward easing expectations.

events.title: US September PCE inflation
events.why_it_matters: Core PCE is the Fed's preferred gauge and follows a hot September CPI; a 3%+ core print would harden the December hike case.
events.what_to_watch: Core PCE m/m and supercore services; any upside surprise lifts front-end yields and hits duration-sensitive equities.

events.title: ECB October meeting — pause expected, December hike in view
events.why_it_matters: The ECB is expected to hold the deposit rate at 2.50% after two summer hikes, but officials have signalled a third increase is likely in December.
events.what_to_watch: Lagarde's guidance on December and any pushback against market pricing of a hike.

events.title: Bank of Japan October meeting — hold at 1.25%, inflation forecast upgrade likely
events.why_it_matters: The BoJ is expected to pause after last month's hike but may raise its inflation assessment toward 2%, keeping a December hike live and supporting the yen.
events.what_to_watch: Ueda's press conference and the quarterly outlook; a hawkish hold would steepen JGBs and strengthen JPY.

events.title: Bank of Korea decision — hold at 3.00%, November hike expected
events.why_it_matters: All 34 Reuters economists expect a hold after two consecutive hikes, but guidance on November matters for KRW and Korean tech-heavy assets.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the BOK explicitly signals a November hike; KRW and KOSPI sensitivity to chip-cycle commentary.

events.title: Japan September national CPI
events.why_it_matters: Headline CPI is expected to accelerate to ~2.1% on energy and a weak yen, reinforcing the case for a December BoJ hike.
events.what_to_watch: Core-core inflation and services prices; a hot print would lift JGB yields and JPY.

events.title: China October manufacturing PMI
events.why_it_matters: September PMI was 50.1 and October consensus is ~50.3; a break below 50 would revive stimulus expectations and pressure industrial commodities.
events.what_to_watch: New export orders and production sub-indices; weakness would reinforce the two-speed China narrative.

events.title: US October ISM manufacturing
events.why_it_matters: Manufacturing has been a soft spot; a print near the 54.5 prior would confirm the economy is holding up despite high rates.
events.what_to_watch: New orders and employment sub-indices; a drop below 52 would add to growth concerns ahead of the December Fed meeting.

events.title: US Conference Board consumer confidence
events.why_it_matters: Michigan sentiment has fallen to a 15-year low, and the Conference Board print will show whether the labour-market view is deteriorating ahead of the holiday season.
events.what_to_watch: Expectations and labour differential; a weak print would hurt discretionary retail and support duration.

events.title: Brazil presidential runoff — Bolsonaro vs Lula
events.why_it_matters: Flávio Bolsonaro led the first round and polls, and a runoff win would extend the market-friendly rally in Brazilian assets; a Lula comeback would reverse it.
events.what_to_watch: Final polls and turnout in Sao Paulo; Ibovespa, BRL and Petrobras reaction.

events.title: US midterm elections
events.why_it_matters: Prediction markets put a Democratic sweep at roughly two-in-three, which would reshape expectations for AI regulation, bank oversight, healthcare policy and fiscal spending.
events.what_to_watch: Senate and House control; a sweep would hit banks and AI giants while boosting healthcare and clean energy.

events.title: OPEC+ monthly meeting — production held for November
events.why_it_matters: OPEC+ has held November production steady after completing prior increases, and with Hormuz risk premium elevated the meeting could tighten or loosen the market.
events.what_to_watch: Compliance language and any hint of retaliatory supply action if Iran disruptions worsen.

events.title: Strait of Hormuz attacks and oil-supply risk
events.why_it_matters: More than a dozen strikes on shipping since late September have reduced transit volumes and kept crude above $100, a direct tax on the global economy.
events.what_to_watch: Whether attacks escalate to a closure or major tanker loss; Brent above $120 would force a broader risk-off.

events.title: Venezuela–Guyana Essequibo dispute escalates
events.why_it_matters: Venezuela has authorised oil exploration in disputed waters and Exxon is pressing ahead, while the US has warned Caracas against attacking Guyana or Exxon assets.
events.what_to_watch: Any military incident or Exxon evacuation; a disruption would add a second oil-risk premium.

events.title: EU long-term budget impasse after October summit
events.why_it_matters: EU leaders ended the summit without a breakthrough on the next multiannual budget, leaving energy support and Ukraine funding unresolved.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a special summit is called before year-end; failure raises fragmentation risk in EU assets.

events.title: UK Autumn Budget — bank tax in focus
events.why_it_matters: Chancellor Healey's first Budget is expected to avoid raising capital gains tax and instead target banks to fill a fiscal gap, with gilt and sterling sensitivity high.
events.what_to_watch: Bank surcharge and fiscal headroom; a bigger-than-expected bank levy hits UK bank shares and could steepen gilts.

events.title: China restricts export of AI and chip-design technologies
events.why_it_matters: Beijing added 23 AI technologies to its export-control list and imposed immediate registration on outbound frontier models and chip IP, escalating tech fragmentation.
events.what_to_watch: The November 15 registration deadline and whether Washington retaliates with tighter semiconductor equipment controls.

events.title: US Section 301 China exclusions expire November 10
events.why_it_matters: 178 product exclusions expire and no extension has been announced, which would raise costs for importers just as the broader truce runs to January 10, 2027.
events.what_to_watch: A last-minute USTR extension; failure would hit hardware and industrial importers with retroactive tariff exposure.

events.title: US–China trade truce extended to January 10, 2027
events.why_it_matters: The two-month extension removes the immediate November 10 cliff and keeps the 100% tariff threat off the table through the holiday season.
events.what_to_watch: Implementation of the '30-for-30' reciprocal tariff cuts and whether China's new export controls derail the truce.

events.title: Tesla Q3 earnings
events.why_it_matters: EV demand, margins and any robotaxi/autonomy update will set the tone for the EV complex and the Musk premium after a sharp tech selloff.
events.what_to_watch: Automotive gross margin and energy-storage growth; a margin miss could drag the whole high-beta complex.

events.title: Meta Q3 earnings
events.why_it_matters: AI capex guidance and ad demand will test whether investors will tolerate another year of heavy spending after the Nasdaq's worst week since April 2025.
events.what_to_watch: Capex guide for 2027 and Reels/WhatsApp monetisation; a capex raise without revenue upside is the bear case.

events.title: Microsoft and Alphabet Q3 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Azure and Google Cloud growth, plus AI monetisation and capex, are the single biggest test of the AI trade this earnings season.
events.what_to_watch: Azure constant-currency growth and Google Cloud margin; a beat could reverse the October tech selloff.

events.title: Apple and Amazon Q3 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Apple's iPhone holiday guide and Amazon's AWS growth and retail margin will show whether the consumer and cloud capex cycle are holding up.
events.what_to_watch: Apple's December-quarter revenue guide and AWS operating margin; weak consumer commentary would hit discretionary retail.

events.title: Samsung Electronics full Q3 results
events.why_it_matters: Preliminary guidance showed a record ~$80bn operating profit on AI memory demand, and the divisional breakdown will confirm whether the HBM cycle still has legs.
events.what_to_watch: HBM revenue mix and capex plans; a cautious memory outlook would hit the Korean chip complex and SK Hynix.

events.title: Coordinated global port strike
events.why_it_matters: Dockworkers across more than 100 ports plan a coordinated strike, threatening container flows and adding to supply-chain inflation just as holiday shipments peak.
events.what_to_watch: Participation at Los Angeles/Long Beach, Rotterdam and Piraeus; a multi-day stoppage would lift freight rates and hit retailers.

events.title: AI/tech valuation selloff
events.why_it_matters: The Nasdaq had its worst week since April 2025 on AI capex and valuation concerns, and the drawdown is still live heading into mega-cap earnings.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Microsoft/Alphabet earnings stabilise the complex or confirm a deeper de-rating; breadth and credit spreads are the tell.

events.title: China October LPR decision — held at 3.0%/3.5%
events.why_it_matters: The LPR was unchanged for a 17th month, signalling the PBOC is prioritising bank margins and a policy-rate overhaul over near-term stimulus.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the PBOC shifts its policy anchor to the overnight reverse repo, which would change how markets price Chinese easing.

events.title: Netflix Q3 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Ad-tier engagement and pricing trends set the tone for streaming margins and the media complex into year-end.
events.what_to_watch: Ad-supported subscriber mix and free-cash-flow guide; a miss would weigh on communication services.

events.title: Hurricane Isaias — Gulf Coast landfall, now post-tropical
events.why_it_matters: The first Atlantic hurricane of the season made landfall on the Gulf Coast and disrupted some oil/gas and refining operations, but has since weakened.
events.what_to_watch: Insurance loss estimates and any lingering refinery outages; the storm is no longer a market driver.

events.title: UAW strike ends with tentative GM deal
events.why_it_matters: The tentative deal removes a supply-chain disruption for GM and reduces the risk of contagion to other automakers.
events.what_to_watch: Ratification vote and whether the deal sets a costly pattern for Ford and Stellantis.

top_risks: FOMC hawkish hold and explicit December hike signal — front-end yields rise, hitting long-duration tech and rate-sensitive housing.
Strait of Hormuz escalation to a closure or major tanker loss — Brent above $120 would trigger broad risk-off and inflation repricing.
Mega-cap AI earnings disappoint on capex without revenue — Microsoft/Alphabet/Apple/Amazon could extend the October tech selloff.
Democratic midterm sweep — bank and AI regulation risk premia rise, healthcare rallies, fiscal policy uncertainty increases.
China AI/chip export controls and Section 301 expiry — tech supply-chain fragmentation and tariff-cost surprises.
top_opportunities: Dovish Fed hold plus soft Q3 GDP — a goldilocks print could reverse the October de-rating in growth stocks.
Microsoft/Alphabet earnings beat on Azure and Cloud — would restore confidence in the AI capex cycle.
Brazil runoff relief rally if Bolsonaro wins — Ibovespa, BRL and Petrobras upside.
BoJ hawkish hold with inflation upgrade — yen strength and JGB steepener for macro traders.
UK Budget clarity with no CGT hike — gilt relief and UK bank shares if the bank levy is smaller than feared.
summary: Markets enter the final week of October with the Fed expected to hold but December hike risk live, mega-cap AI earnings and a Democratic midterm sweep in focus, and oil above $100 on Strait of Hormuz attacks. The US-China truce extension removes the November 10 cliff, but China's new AI export controls and the Section 301 expiry keep tech supply-chain risk elevated.
